props.name: design rules

evidence.quote: These comparisons indicate that the present precursor-level strategy—bimetallic Zn/Co dilution combined with DCD-assisted

props.scope: Co–N–C catalysts in the kinetically controlled region
props.statement: The 76 mV dec−1 Tafel slope of CoNC-900 indicates fast initial electron transfer with the proton-coupled formation of *COOH controlling the overall CO2-to-CO rate.

props.name: volcanoes

evidence.quote: Two volcano-type relationships emerge from the controlled series.

props.statement: Two volcano-type relationships govern the performance: one in pyrolysis temperature (CoNC-900 optimally balances conductivity and nitrogen retention) and one in Co feed ratio (10 mol% maximizes accessible Co–Nx density without aggregation).

Four model sites were constructed on a 5 × 5 graphene supercell with 15 Å vacuum: a Co–N4 moiety (Co substituting C, coordinated by four pyridinic N), an edge pyridinic- N site, a bulk graphitic-N site, and pristine graphene.

The potential limiting step is the first proton coupled electron transfer to form COOH, whose free energy barrier is vastly different on Co–N4, 0.42 eV, compared to the other metal-free sites, 1.79 eV, 2.24 eV, and 3.15 eV at U = 0 V, and this point directly explains why the FE_ CO of NC-900 is only 37.6% whereas it is nearly 95% for CoNC-900.

Again, the CO adsorption energy on Co–N4 is not particularly high (−0.72 eV), which explains why CO desorption is only slightly endothermic, in contrast to the relatively strongly CO-bound metals, which exhibit the site poisoning that would be expected given their shallower d-band center −1.17 eV compared with −1.35 eV for Co–N4).

Bader charge analysis reveals a substantial transfer of 0.38 e to the adsorbed *COOH intermediate on Co–N4, together with electron accumulation between the Co centre and the carboxyl carbon, identifying Co as the electron-donating anchor that stabilizes the bent CO2-derived intermediate.

The model Co–N4 (Figure 9b) predicts a density of states with the center of the Co 3d band at −1.35 eV, inside the range corresponding to medium-strength binding, which is a compromise between COOH stabilization and CO release.

evidence.quote: of the CO2-saturated current for the CoNC series (15% for CoNC- 900), compared with 69% for NC-900 and 89% for CB-Vulcan, confirming that the CO2-dependent current arises from CO2 reduction on the Co-containing catalysts rather than from hydrogen evolution.

evidence.note: the recorded fractions are ratios of the N2-saturated to CO2-saturated LSV currents at −0.75 V read from Figure 6a (a current comparison, not a separate potentiostatic electrolysis); the N2 curve is shown for CoNC-900 only; N2 controls for all seven samples are in Supplementary Figure S8, which was not examined
